title.narrative: Cabo Verde: Second Resilient and Equitable Recovery DPF with a Cat DDO

description.narrative: The program development objective is to support the Government's efforts to strengthen the foundations for a resilient and equitable economic recovery through (i) reducing fiscal risks and improving debt transparency; (ii) strengthening the resilience of poor and vulnerable households to climate shocks; and (iii) enabling a sustainable private sector-led recovery.

title.narrative: Result Indicator #8: New tourism investment projects approved in ZDTIs, in compliance with the corresponding POTs and with approved environmental impact assessments (% of total nbr of new ZDTI)

comment.narrative: The overarching regulatory framework governing the investment in tourism development zones (ZDTIs) continues to evolve, as authorities approved a Tourism Zoning Plan (POT) for the Mangue Monte Negro ZDTI in Santiago Island in Aug 2024, as well as a detailed Zoning Plan for the Maio ZDTI in late October 2024. In addition, complementary regulations for local accommodations, synergetic with the overarching decree licensing requirements for tourism accommodation operators (and supported as a PA within the ongoing DPF series) have been approved. Though no new investments have broken ground in ZDTIs since the last reporting in Dec 2023, the forthcoming pipeline is robust as authorities have issued 44 Tourism Utility Statutes for tourism-themed investments since 2022, all under different phases of approval and premised on an approved EIA. The fragmented institutional framework where multiple entities are now overseeing the ZDTIs represents a challenge for consolidated investment screening.

title.narrative: Result Indicator #6: Additional households identified using the social registry that are from the two poorest quintiles

comment.narrative: The 1st supervision mission reviewed progress made on the PRH, which is the target group for the ongoing World Bank sectoral project. While this provided important insights, the actual indicator is the CSU. The 2nd supervision mission shows that, as of Oct 2024, the registry contains comprehensive data of over 90,666 households (over 330,800 people; 66 % of Cabo Verde's population and one of the largest in the region) and ranks them according to their estimated welfare status. In 2021, an additional 18,524 households were registered into the CSU, of which 10,262 belong to the two poorest quintiles (group I and II). In 2022, an additional 6,088 households were registered, of which 3,858 from groups I and II; and in 2023 additional 5,718 households were registered, of which 2,204 from groups I and II. As such, by December 2023, there were 30,330 new registries in the CSU, of which 16,324 from groups I and II. This represents 53 percent and hence the indicator was met at the end of 2023.

title.narrative: Result Indicator #3: Share of annual average loss from disaster and climate-related risks covered under the existing risk financing instruments

comment.narrative: There are two instruments available to cover annual average losses from disaster and climate-related risks which were estimated to US$18.2M in 2019. One of them is the FNE (approximately USD 2M in 2024 and USD 2.2M committed for 2025) and the other is the Cat DDO (USD 10 M). The Fiscal Risk Statement was published on the MoF website with the budget proposal for 2025, which only included the quantification of annual average losses from drought and flood risks (this quantification was undertaken with the support of IMF). The Risk Management unit is working on quantifying also annual average losses linked to volcanic, seismic and sea-level rise risk It was agreed for consistency to continue using the baseline of 2020, which estimated losses at USD 18,2Mas reported in FRS for 2024. The development of a strategy would help identifying other financial instruments adapted to the Cabo Verde context and needs, to mobilize in the future different instruments that would cover different risks.

title.narrative: Result Indicator #7: Improved ELECTRAâ€™s commercial operational performance: Overall system losses

comment.narrative: This indicator is also monitored under the Renewable Energy and Improved Utilities Performance Project (P170236). During the recent mid-term review (October 2024), the end target for this indicator has been revised upwards from 18 percent to 21 percent by December 2026, due to delays in the implementation of the privatization process. Therefore, it is likely that for period of implementation of the program under this DPF, the final value of the indicator will be higher than expected (estimated at 22 percent), though the commitment remains to meet the target of 22 percent by end of 2026.

title.narrative: Result Indicator #2: Support to SOEs (capitalization, guarantees, on-lending) above what is established in the annual budget (percentage)

comment.narrative: The authorities have made efforts to keep support to SOEs, in the form of capitalizations, guarantees and on-lending, in line with the amounts planned in the annual budgets. Based on the data shared by the authorities, support to SOEs has remained within the budgeted amounts in 2021, 2022 and 2023. The authorities have also lowered the ceiling on the issuance of guarantees to SOEs from USD 70 million in 2020 to USD 46 million in 2023 â€“ though it is important to note that, consistent with the Budget Law, restructured loans/guarantees do not count against this limit. Notably, while on-lending and guarantees issued have remained relatively stable, capitalizations to SOE have increased almost three-fold between the 2020 and 2022 period â€“ with a large share going towards the national airline and NewCo (the special purposes vehicle created in 2019 to absorb the national airlineâ€™s debt). In 2023, the overall support to SOEs was 6 percent lower than what was budgeted.

title.narrative: Result Indicator #4: Femaleheaded households benefitting from temporary income support in response to shocks, including climate-related, through emergency cash transfer programs (cumulative number)

comment.narrative: Between 2023 and 2024 there was no allocation of the Emergency Social Inclusion Income (rendimento social de InclusÃ£o emergencial - RSIE), as no crisis mechanism was activated. However, with the regulation of this emergency social benefit, the country has now a legal instrument to provide social assistance to families in times of crisis. The main challenge would be the timely availability of resources for the RSIE in case of need, as it is not foreseen in the annual budget. However, it would be possible to reallocate it quickly from other funds such as the Fundo MAIS, the Sovereign Fund and the funds allocated by the Ministry of Finance. In 2024, the regular RSI benefited 8,835 households (635 funded by the State Budget and 8,200 through the Fundo MAIS).

title.narrative: Result Indicator #9: Total investments generated in aquaculture â€“ cumulative (USD million)

comment.narrative: The current investments in both onshore and offshore aquaculture in Cabo Verde continue to mature enabled by the necessary regulatory by-laws supported under the DPF. The sector remains anchored on two projects â€“ the first inception investment on an onshore shrimp farm (Fazenda do CamarÃ£o) from the early 2010s, and more recently in 2021, Nortuna (a Norwegian-led project), for an onshore and offshore project. Both projects are based in SÃ£o Vicente Island, and the latter continues to expand investments, with the first phase of R&D now complete and the first commercial pilot production of Esmoregal (Seriola rivoliana), an eligible species approved under the ministerial order, undergoing pilot comercial test trials in late 2024.

title.narrative: Result Indicator #5: FNE audit report produced and published by the Court of Account including evaluation of drought response expenditures (yes/no).

comment.narrative:
The FNE has not been activated for drought-related response since the new bylaws were adopted. The FNE was used to respond to the state of contingency declared in SÃ£o Vicente in 2022 (30 M CVE), to the state of calamity declared in 2023 in Fogo and Brava (150 M CVE), and the state of contingency for the Dengue emergency in 2024 (15 M CVE).
The external control process includes, in addition to the audit carried out by the General Inspection of Finances (IGF) in accordance with the terms of the Procedures Manual and the Law, an assessment by the Court of Auditors when the FNE will presents its accounts for the year 2023. The FNE sent in 2024 the accounts to the Court of Accounts, which is currently in the process of reviewing these. The audit report is expected for the first semester of 2025.
The 2024 national budget included an allocation of 205 M CVE for the FNE, and the 2025 national budget includes an allocation of 224 M CVE for the FNE.

title.narrative: Result Indicator #1: Sectoral coverage score in the World Bank debt reporting heat map

comment.narrative: Consistent with the requirements of the Regulatory decree No. 40/2022, the authorities expanded the content of the 2022 Annual Debt Report to include consolidated debt of nonfinancial public sector â€“ including SOEs and municipalities. As a result, Cabo Verdeâ€™s sectoral coverage score in the World Bank debt reporting heat map moved from â€œpartialâ€ to â€œfullâ€ for the 2022 assessment â€“meeting the results indicator target ahead of time. The 2023 assessment maintains this rating. The timeliness of reporting has also remained consistent with best practice. Building on recommendations from the 1st supervision mission, debt transparency has been further enhanced through the inclusion of complete information on recent loan agreements in the 2023 Annual Public Debt Report. However, important steps remain to be taken with regards to transparency of debt management, including publishing of the MTDS and complementing ABP - this would also contribute to improve the score in CPIA (economic pillar).
